summary: The screened Friday arXiv window is strongest on hypernuclear production in RHIC isobar data, constrained small-x nuclear saturation inference, and practical but still immature agentic/representation-learning workflows for collider and heavy-ion physics. Key themes are hypertriton wave-function sensitivity, coalescence versus thermal expectations, physics-informed BK evolution, nuclear dipole amplitudes, autonomous CLVisc hydrodynamics, lightweight collider pretraining, causal time-series benchmarking, and graph-search AI for theoretical physics.
strongest_paper: 2607.28113: Probing (Hyper)Nuclei Wave Functions and Production Mechanisms in sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV Isobar Collisions at RHIC
top_takeaway: The strongest science is STAR's hypernuclei/coalescence result and the constrained CGC neural extraction; the most transferable AI/ML work is useful but should be judged by physics constraints, uncertainty handling, and domain-shift validation rather than by agent or foundation-model labels.

papers.title: Probing (Hyper)Nuclei Wave Functions and Production Mechanisms in sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV Isobar Collisions at RHIC
papers.abstract: STAR reports centrality-dependent production of hypertriton, anti-hypertriton, helium-3, anti-helium-3, and triton in 200 GeV Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions. Ratios deviate from thermal-model expectations and are better described by coalescence calculations using realistic non-Gaussian wave functions.

papers.title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
papers.authors_short: Si-Wei Dai, Haowu Duan, Long-Gang Pang, Guang-You Qin, Shu-Yi Wei, Han-Zhong Zhang, Wenbin Zhao
papers.abstract: The paper embeds collinearly improved BK evolution into a physics-informed neural-network objective to infer the impact-parameter-averaged Pb dipole amplitude from forward-hadron nuclear modification and coherent J/psi photoproduction data, with QCD evolution and positivity enforced.

papers.title: CLVisc Agent for autonomous relativistic hydrodynamics studies
papers.authors_short: Qi Wang, Long-Gang Pang, Shi Pu, Xin-Nian Wang
papers.abstract: The paper demonstrates an LLM-agent workflow that learns CLVisc operations, runs 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic simulations, performs scans, compares results, and generates figures for eta/s and O+O nuclear-structure case studies.

papers.title: Relativistic transport near moving interfaces
papers.abstract: A formal treatment of linear disturbances near moving planar interfaces in relativistic media, unifying boundary layers, wakes, and shock-tail asymptotics through a propagator and mode-selection construction.

papers.title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation
papers.authors_short: Liangyu Wu, Qibin Liu, Alexander Yue, Julia Gonski
papers.abstract: NEXUS pretrains a small autoencoder on charged-particle track features from collider data and fine-tunes for kinematic regression and event classification with limited labels, with additional demonstrations on other scientific domains.

papers.title: DoTime: A Synthetic Benchmark Generator for Interventional and Counterfactual Time Series
papers.authors_short: Dennis Thumm, Billy Tim Anthony, Ying Chen
papers.abstract: DoTime creates temporal structural causal model benchmarks with interventions, counterfactuals, regime switches, nonstationarity, and exact ground truth for evaluating causal time-series models.

papers.title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
papers.authors_short: Jonathan J. Heckman, Shani Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Gary Shiu
papers.abstract: The paper trains transformers and MLPs, aided by pathfinder algorithms, to trace Seiberg dualities in supersymmetric quiver gauge theories, reporting improved search efficiency for modest quiver sizes.

cautions.title: Photon-calibrated event-activity bias and subcollision geometry in d+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV with PYTHIA 8 Angantyr
cautions.authors_short: Muhammad Ajaz, Haifa I. Alrebdi, Muhammad Waqas
cautions.abstract: A PYTHIA 8 Angantyr generator-level study of hard-event activity bias in d+Au collisions using photons, pions, and jets. The abstract notes that the calculation does not identify a unique microscopic origin for residual correlations.
